findings.summary: Implementer report states 'Tests for the change were written and run,' but the diff contains no test file, and the repo has zero test infrastructure anywhere (no vitest/jest, no `test` script in root or apps/web package.json, no *.test.*/*.spec.* files exist in the tree). The claim cannot be true as stated. I independently verified the plugin's core behavior by feeding it a synthetic mdast tree built from real repo content (a link to the currently-draft 'the-weekend-deploy' post plus a link to a published post) and confirmed it strips the draft link to plain text, leaves the published link intact, and logs the expected per-file warning — so the code itself works, but the report's testing claim is fabricated.

findings.summary: The site's actual isPublished() (apps/web/src/utils/data-utils.ts:12-16) short-circuits with `import.meta.env.DEV` so future-dated (non-draft) posts read as published while running `astro dev`. This plugin's isPublished() has no such bypass, so during local dev a cross-link to a future-dated post gets stripped to plain text here while every listing/RSS/tag page elsewhere on the site still shows that same post as live — a minor divergence from 'the same rule the rest of the site applies', though it self-corrects in production builds.

findings.summary: loadArticles() uses a non-recursive readdirSync(ARTICLES_DIR), but the actual blog collection loader in content.config.ts uses a recursive glob (`**/*.{md,mdx}`). If articles are ever organized into subdirectories, this plugin would fail to find those slugs; articles.get(slug) would return undefined, isPublished(undefined) returns false, and valid links to genuinely-published posts in a subdirectory would be silently stripped. No impact today since packages/content/articles/ is currently flat.
